section.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains the phrase "I came to My garden" from the Midrash, focusing on the precise meaning of "Shechinah" and its root in the revelation of Ein Sof.
section.t: "I came to My garden, My sister, My bride"2,
and it is brought in Midrash Rabbah
(in its place3)
"It does not say 'to the garden' but 'to My garden,'
to My private garden,
to the place which was My essential [dwelling] initially,
for the essential Shechinah was in the lower realms."
End of quote.
And to understand the precise wording "essential Shechinah,"
behold, in the explanation of "Shechinah," the Alter Rebbea explains
that it is called Shechinah because it dwells and is enclothed,
from the term "and I will dwell in their midst"4,
which is the beginning of the revelation of Ein Sof.
And from what he writes5
that the beginning of the revelation of Ein Sof is called by the name Shechinah,
it is understood from this that the concept of Shechinah is also far above Atzilus,
even in the aspect of the light before the tzimtzum,
for the beginning of revelation is in the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum,
and as the Mitteler Rebbe wroteb
that the illumination of the line and thread relative to the essentiality of Ein Sof is called by the name Shechinah.
For the concept of Shechinah is in every place according to its context.
Regarding Atzilus, Malchus is called by the name Shechinah.
And also in this, that Malchus of Atzilus is called Shechinah, the Tzemach Tzedekc explains
that this is specifically when it becomes an aspect of Atik for the world of Beriah,
but when it is in Atzilus it is unified with them
(with the Sefiros of Atzilus)
and the term Shechinah does not apply.
Nevertheless, this does not contradict what was said above that the line is called by the name Shechinah,
for the Shechinah mentioned in the words of our sages is Malchus of Atzilus,
and even this is only when it specifically becomes an aspect of Atik for Beriah,
but in its root,
that is, as it is relative to Ein Sof,
behold, even the line is called by the name Shechinah.
And one of the reasons why the line is called by the name Shechinah relative to Ein Sof,
the Rebbe Maharashd wrote
is that the line, the intent of its drawing down is in order to be enclothed in the worlds and souls of Israel,
therefore, even at its beginning it is called by the name Shechinah.
And higher still, the Shechinah in its first root above the tzimtzum,
the Rebbe, of blessed memorye, explains
that the revelation of the light as it is before the tzimtzum,
is called by the name Shechinah.
For in the general light before the tzimtzum there are three levels,
the essence of the light and the spreading forth of the light,
and in the spreading forth of the light there are two levels: the revelation of the light as it is for itself, which is the source of the light of Sovev,
and the revelation of the light for itself that relates to the worlds, which is the source of the light of Memaleh,
and this revelation of light is called by the name Shechinah.
And even though it is before the tzimtzum and it is impossible for it to be a source for worlds,
which is why the tzimtzum was necessary,
and the first tzimtzum is specifically in the aspect of withdrawal,
nevertheless, it is called by the name Shechinah.
And this is the precise wording "the essential Shechinah was in the lower realms,"
that is, the revelation of the Shechinah in the lower realms
is not the Shechinah as it is relative to Atzilus,
that is, Malchus,
nor as it is relative to Ein Sof,
that is, the line,
but rather the essence and pnimiyus of the Shechinah was specifically in the lower realms,
for the light
that is enclothed in the worlds comes in order and gradation.
And above, it shines with greater revelation,
and the more it is drawn down and descends, the light diminishes.
And so it is in general regarding the light of the order of hishtalshelus.
And even though before the sin there was also below the light in revelation,
nevertheless, even then the revelation of the light was greater above.
And as our sages said*vi,
"He extended His right hand and created the heavens, He extended His left hand and created the earth."
Rather, the intent is regarding the light that is above the worlds,
the essential Shechinah.
